How JavaScript runs in the browser

JavaScript is a programming language that runs inside the browser. This guide explains how scripts are parsed, scheduled, and executed, and why a document that mentions JavaScript is still ordinary readable documentation. It covers parsing, the event loop, task scheduling, and the rendering steps that follow script execution.

Readers who want to enable JavaScript in their own browser can do so from the settings page. The remainder of this article discusses rendering performance, deferred scripts, module loading, and the interaction between the parser and the network stack.
